measurer_summary.question: A1: timestamp granularity and semantics (the latency gate). Pair each call with its first result on (session_id, call_id) and take delta = parse_ts(result) - parse_ts(call). Report the stamp and delta resolution per corpus, per swechat format and per is_subagent. Check event time against insert time (aiv_cc, aiv_cu), look for human-wait evidence in the Claude Code formats, and apply the kill rule: whole-second stamps, or a stamp shared by call and result, mean latency analysis is dead.

per_corpus.answer: Stamps are milliseconds (57,496/57,496 stamps have 3 digits; the last digit is uniform). 13,589 pairs over 126 sessions. Identical call/result stamps: 37 (0.272% [0.128, 0.484]). Whole-second stamps: 0.096% [0.062, 0.131]. Negative deltas: 0. Delta p50 0.101 s [0.069, 0.142], p95 30.1 s, max 78,675.7 s (a subagent call). Main-thread p50 0.133 s (n 9,679); subagent p50 0.048 s (n 3,910, 52 sessions). Human waits are clearly present: 13.2% [6.8, 21.7] of Edit/Write calls take more than 2 s; 34/126 sessions (27.0% [20.0, 35.3]) contain a user tool rejection, which arrives p50 23.4 s after the call; 15.0% [7.2, 26.9] of long shell commands start more than 2 s after the call (bash_progress offset). All 3,178 PreToolUse hook stamps fall inside the call-to-result window.
per_corpus.decisive_number: identical stamps 0.272% [0.128, 0.484] of 13,589 pairs; whole-second stamps 0.096%

Millisecond event stamps. 5,164 pairs over 107 sessions; 0 identical, 0 negative. Delta p50 0.247 s [0.102, 0.351]. Where the tool reports its own duration, the stamps bracket it tightly: Glob delta minus durationMs p50 0.010 s, never negative (427/427). No sign of human waits on edits: 0/358 Edit/Write calls exceed 2 s (max 0.09 s). The 173 permission denials (67/107 sessions, 62.6% [53.2, 71.2]) are automatic (p50 7 ms, max 37 ms). There are no hook_progress events. Shell calls cannot be split into execution time and waiting (26.1% exceed 2 s).

Microsecond database row-insert stamps (the last digit is uniform, chi2 p 0.89). 33,475 pairs over 77 sessions; 0 identical, 0 negative; 33,001 distinct delta values. Insert time tracks event time and is not batched: 0 of 113,019 consecutive-row gaps are under 1 ms, and the smallest gap is 18.2 ms. Run spans match the SDK's own duration_ms (82 runs, p50 difference -3.7 ms). However, every call-to-result delta has a floor of about 50 ms that does not depend on the tool: TodoWrite p1 is 0.0516 s against 0.001 s in swechat; read p1 0.0582 s against 0.002 s; the overall minimum is 0.046 s. Glob delta minus its reported durationMs is p50 0.049 s. All 125 runs use bypassPermissions, so there are no human waits. A separate trap: a call that is not the last tool_use block of its message absorbs the generation time of the later blocks (Write p50 15.5 s for non-last blocks vs 0.089 s for last blocks). The parent_uuid check could not be done: parent_uuid is null on all 113,144 rows.

per_corpus.answer: Call and result share one stamp in 6,107/6,107 pairs (199 sessions), in all 10 strata. Weaker quantities remain. The inter-turn gap is p50 14.06 s [13.26, 14.92] (n 6,255). For Gemini only (1,161 gaps, 35 sessions), the gap minus server timing is p50 6.36 s and is never negative. created_at minus the HTTP Date header is p50 4.49 s, but the Date header is whole-second, so that per-action proxy is also dead under the kill rule. updated_at is within 1 ms of created_at in 6,104/6,107 rows and adds nothing.
No timestamps anywhere: 0 of 353 pairs have a stamp (ts_kind none on all 1,733 rows).

surprises: aiv_cc: every tool's call-to-result delta has a floor of about 50 ms, the same for TodoWrite and Bash. Inserts are never closer than 18.2 ms apart, and none are batched (0 of 113,019 gaps under 1 ms). The floor is an additive offset that also appears against tool-reported durations (Glob +49 ms); it does not coarsen the resolution.

aiv_cc: a call that is not the last tool_use block of its API message absorbs the generation time of the later blocks (Write p50 15.5 s vs 0.089 s). In the CLI corpora the opposite holds: the result usually arrives before the last block is stamped (cc_local shell 87.2%, swechat reads 80.7%), so tool execution streams in the CLI but not in this SDK version.
swechat Claude Code: 27% of sessions contain a 'user doesn't want to proceed' rejection, arriving p50 23.4 s after the call. That is a direct measure of a human answering a permission prompt.
cc_local: 173 permission denials in 62.6% of sessions are automatic (p50 7 ms). The same marker means machine denial in cc_local and human interaction in swechat.
swechat WebFetch delta exceeds its own reported durationMs by p50 1.68 s (p95 88.6 s); in cc_local the excess is 0.004 s. This is consistent with per-domain permission prompts.
Gemini (swechat) has 6 negative deltas and a p1 floor of 58 ms, so its message-level call stamp is not the moment the call was emitted.
aiv_cu's last-digit uniformity test gives a spurious p = 0.009 when the shared stamp is counted twice; on distinct stamps p = 0.28.
implications_for_phase_b: The latency probe can use swechat claude_code (126 sessions), cc_local (107) and aiv_cc (77). aiv_cu, whowhen and Cursor are out. Codex (15 sessions), OpenCode (25), Gemini (10) and Copilot (2) pass the gate on stamp granularity but are too small for per-format baselines.

Proposed rule for calls with no human wait (not applied):
- Stamped pairs in an ALIVE unit only.
- Tool class auto_read (read/glob/grep/ls) or internal_noperm (todo/task*/toolsearch). The one exception is aiv_cc, which runs bypassPermissions: there every tool qualifies except human-interactive and subagent tools.
- The call must be the last or only tool_use block of its API message.
- No cc_permission_denied or cc_interrupt_reject marker on the result.
- No linked PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook_progress event (swechat) or hook attachment (cc_local).
aiv_cc deltas below about 0.1 s are bounded by the ingestion floor. Only compare tools well above about 50 ms there; a tool-independent ~50 ms offset is present.

Shell, edit, write and web tools in swechat claude_code and cc_local are not clean latencies. This holds until permissionMode is carried into the IR. Where bash_progress exists, the pre-exec offset measures the wait directly.
Keep Codex tool_raw values apart (shell_command / exec_command / write_stdin); polling and yield semantics put fixed-value spikes into delta.
Phase B's first count should be how many calls the proposed rule keeps, per corpus and tool class. A1 did not measure this.
could_not_measure: aiv_cc 'event ts < parent_uuid ts': parent_uuid is null on all 113,144 IR rows. Only the causal proxy was measured: 0 results stamped before their call.
permissionMode for swechat claude_code and cc_local: it is in the raw entries but not carried by the IR. Loader/lib edits were out of scope.
Whether OpenCode time.start/time.end include permission-prompt waits.
Hook durations in cc_local: no hook_progress events; only 23 hook attachments, linked to 10 calls.
Server-timing residuals for any aiv_cu model other than Gemini (timing exists only for gemini-pro and gemini-flash, 35 sessions).
Stable per-format latency baselines outside Claude Code (10 to 25 sessions per format; Copilot 2).

overclaims: '27% of sessions contain a user doesn't want to proceed rejection ... a direct measure of a human answering a permission prompt.' The 34/126 counts every cc_interrupt_reject result. 1 of the 59 is '[Request interrupted' (only 33 sessions have the quoted text), and 18/59 are on ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion, which are plan approvals and questions, not permission prompts. Counting only permission-gated tools: 41 results in 20/126 sessions = 15.9% [10.5, 23.2]. The minimum latency is 0.164 s.

'The same marker means machine denial in cc_local and human interaction in swechat.' This is wrong; the two corpora use different markers for these. cc_permission_denied is machine-fast in both: swechat n 3, p50 0.022 s, max 0.037; cc_local n 173, p50 0.007 s. cc_interrupt_reject is human-paced in both: swechat p50 23.4 s; cc_local 9 results, p50 4.9 s. What differs between the corpora is frequency, not meaning.

Notes Part 2 says human-wait evidence is 'absent in aiv_cc and cc_local'. For cc_local the probe's own JSON shows 9 cc_interrupt_reject results in 6/107 sessions (5.6% [2.6, 11.7]), p50 4.9 s, 6 of them shell. Only 'no waits on Edit/Write' (0/358) is supported.

aiv_cc: 'a call that is not the last tool_use block of its message absorbs the generation time of the later blocks ... tool execution streams in the CLI but not in this SDK version.' 160 of the 165 not-last file_write calls come from 1 session. For other tools, not-last results usually arrive before the last block's stamp: grep 41/41, read 45/68, get_events 502/993, chat_message 187/294, shell 549/1,570. Not-last Read is faster than last (p50 0.111 vs 0.314 s). Execution evidently does stream in the SDK for most tools; this is a one-session Write effect.

aiv_cc: 'That is the ingestion floor' and 'insert time tracks event time'. The minimum inter-row gap is 18.2 ms, so inserts alone can be that close, while call-to-result is never under 46 ms. The ~50 ms is a pipeline floor of unidentified cause. The match with event time is shown only at run level: 82 run spans vs SDK duration_ms, p50 -3.7 ms, p5 -0.244 s, p95 0.128 s. Per-event insert lag is unmeasured. The 'additive offset' also varies (Glob excess p5 0.019 to p50 0.049 s, 1/90 negative), so it is not a constant.

'15% of long shell commands start more than 2 s after the call (bash_progress offset).' The 373 calls include 6 Task (subagent) calls linked through parent_call_id. All 6 are over 2 s (p50 68.9 s), and that is subagent run time, not a pre-exec wait. Shell only: 50/367 = 13.6% [5.8, 25.9], before the ~1 s rounding from the integer elapsedTimeSeconds.

'Human waits are clearly present: 13.2% [6.8, 21.7] of Edit/Write calls take more than 2 s.' The probe's own recorded reason for the 2 s threshold says it captures human prompts, hooks or slow file systems, so this is not a direct human measure. Hooks do not explain it (182/296 slow edits have no hook event). It is concentrated: 187/296 slow edits sit in 5 sessions, 51/115 sessions have any, and 230/296 are in sessions that also have a rejection. It shows waits in a minority of sessions, not a corpus-wide property.

'The heavy right tails are real waits: the maximum is 78,675.7 s, a subagent.' The maximum is a main-thread Task call (is_subagent False) lasting about 21.9 h, and that subagent's own inner calls also show ~78,443 s deltas. This fits a suspended or resumed session. 'Real waits' is asserted, not measured.
'The last native digit is uniform' is backed by a swechat-pooled chi2 p of 0.20. OpenCode alone, on 8,298 distinct stamps, gives p 0.039. Minor, and it does not affect any verdict.
